info.title: Antifailure control plane
info.description: Environments, runs, verdicts, masking attestations, and network decisions across an organization. The control plane never receives database contents, model traffic, or secrets: it receives events, metadata, and artifacts that were opted in.

Refusal.description: A refusal from a hand-written route. `error` is one sentence for a person, and it names no internal path, table, or query.

retryAfterSeconds.description: Present on 403 and 429. Wait this long before sending the same request again.

ServerFailure.description: The unexpected path. Hono answers an unhandled error with plain text by default, and a caller should not need a second parser exactly when the service is least healthy, so this shape is guaranteed instead.

code.description: A code from the published catalog at https://antifailure.dev/errors.v1.json.

requestId.description: The same value as the x-request-id response header. Quote it when reporting the failure: it is the only thing that ties this answer to a log line, because nothing about the request payload is logged.

TrpcFailure.description: The tRPC error envelope, produced by tRPC rather than by this service. `code` is the JSON-RPC integer; the readable one is `data.code`.

Readiness.description: Served by both the 200 and the 503. `version` and `commit` are what is actually deployed, which is the pair a rollback decision is made on.

reason.description: Present only when ready is false. Why the database did not answer.

get.description: Reports whether the control-plane process is answering. It does not touch the database.

500.description: The request failed for a reason the control plane did not expect. The body carries a correlation id; nothing about the request payload is logged or returned.

get.description: Checks the application database and reports the version and commit that are actually serving.

200.description: The process and its database are ready.

500.description: The request failed for a reason the control plane did not expect. The body carries a correlation id; nothing about the request payload is logged or returned.

503.description: The process is alive and its database did not answer. The body reports the deployed version and commit, which is what a rollback decision needs.

post.description: Authenticated by a per-engine bearer token, not a session. Events are idempotent by id and ordered by sequence within an environment, so a retry is safe and a late arrival does not move an environment backwards. A batch carries at most 500 events.

id.description: Unique within the organization. A repeat is dropped.

type.description: One of x-antifailure-event-types, or a newer type this control plane does not know. An unknown type is stored and projects nothing.

payload.description: Type specific. An environment.* event should carry repository (owner/name) and branch on EVERY event and not only the first, because the environment row is created from whichever event arrives first and an event that cannot name its repository cannot create one. started_at is when the environment began existing, which is not when the event fired: usage and the expiry are measured from it, so an environment reported ready after its build is still billed for the build. ttl_seconds is the declared lifetime, added to that instant to give the expiry.

202.description: Every event was accepted or was a duplicate. An accepted event that changed no environment row carries a note saying why, and is counted in unprojected; it is stored either way.

207.description: Some events were rejected. The outcomes array says which and why.

400.description: The body is not JSON, or it carries no events array. Nothing was stored.

403.description: The token is valid and the organization is suspended. Events are refused rather than dropped, so an engine should keep the batch and send it again after retryAfterSeconds.

413.description: The batch is larger than the limit.

429.description: Too many events. Retry-After says how long to wait before sending the same batch again.

500.description: The request failed for a reason the control plane did not expect. The body carries a correlation id; nothing about the request payload is logged or returned.

post.summary: Exchange a GitHub Actions workflow identity for an engine token
post.description:
How a job in a customer's CI authenticates with no token, no environment variable and no repository secret. The workflow asks GitHub for an identity token with the audience antifailure-control-plane (it needs `id-token: write`), posts it here, and receives an engine token good for 15 minutes on POST /v1/events.

The signature, issuer, audience and expiry are all checked, and none of that is what decides which organization the token belongs to. A signed identity proves which repository a job runs in and nothing about who that repository belongs to, because anybody can run Actions in a repository they own. Access comes from a claim on the repository instead.

Most callers never make that claim themselves. When a repository has no claim and exactly one organization holds a live GitHub App installation on its owner, the claim is created on this first exchange and recorded as having come from the installation. What is refused is a repository with no claim AND no installation to stand in for one: an owner nobody has installed the App on reaches nobody, and an owner two organizations have installed on is refused rather than guessed at. POST /v1/oidc/bindings claims one by hand, for a repository the App is not installed on.

token.description: The workflow identity token, minted for audience antifailure-control-plane.

200.description: An engine token, returned once and stored nowhere. Present it as a bearer token on POST /v1/events exactly as a static one.

400.description: The body is not JSON, or carries no token.

401.description: The identity token did not verify. `reason` is one of malformed, bad_algorithm, no_key, invalid_signature, wrong_issuer, wrong_audience, expired, not_yet_valid, no_repository or keys_unavailable, and `error` is a sentence the workflow author can act on.

403.description: The identity verified and grants nothing. `reason` is no_binding when the repository has not been claimed, binding_revoked when the claim was withdrawn, or installation_suspended.

429.description: Too many exchanges for this repository. A job needs one credential.

400.description: The body is not JSON, or is missing a field.

403.description: The organization is suspended.

404.description: No such environment in this organization.

409.description: This token does not hold the lease.

post.summary: Take the workload run waiting for an environment
post.description: Moves the oldest requested run for the environment to accepted and returns its compiled version, with a lease. Answers 200 and a null run when nothing is waiting, so a poller can tell that apart from a failure. The engine pulls rather than being told because a workflow_dispatch carries only the inputs the workflow declares.

400.description: The body is not JSON, or is missing a field.

403.description: The organization is suspended.

404.description: No such environment in this organization.

409.description: This token does not hold the lease.

post.summary: Say the run is still going
post.description: Extends the lease and the deadline. A run whose deadline passes with nothing said about it ends as abandoned, which is the control plane admitting it never heard rather than a claim that the work failed.

400.description: The body is not JSON, or is missing a field.

403.description: The organization is suspended.

404.description: No such environment in this organization.

409.description: This token does not hold the lease.

post.summary: Take the runtime commands waiting for this organization
post.description: Teardowns and cancellations, with a lease. Reachable while the organization is suspended, deliberately: a suspension stops new work, and stopping what is running is the opposite of new work.

400.description: The body is not JSON, or is missing a field.

403.description: The organization is suspended.

404.description: No such environment in this organization.

409.description: This token does not hold the lease.

post.summary: Say what happened to a command
post.description: Only the holder of the lease may acknowledge, and an acknowledgement that matches no row answers 409 rather than 200: an acknowledgement nobody applied is the silent nothing the durable command exists to end.
